title: Misawa Airmen Perform Bilateral Rescue Operation
description: Air Force Airmen work alongside Japan Air Self Defense Force service members to complete a rescue operation during Northern Viper 17. Senior Airman Jarrod Vickers takes us to Draughon Range.
keywords: PJ, pararescue, USAF, JASDF, operations, rescue, fighter, pilot

transcript.text: (rain splattering)
- [Jarrett] Deep in the forest of Northern Japan,
a handful of Misawa airmen are getting soaked.
But it's all for a good purpose.
- Yeah, we're out here today at the drada range
doing a joint exercise with the JASDF
for an isolated personnel pickup.
So they're gonna send out an Ha 60 and hoist me up
into a helicopter while I simulate having bailed out
of an F-16 and sustained injury through that process.
- [Jarrett] But until that helicopter arrives,
they set up and go over the game plan.
- So as you can probably see behind me,
it's pretty wooded, heavily wooded,
so they cannot land to just walk me onto a helicopter
so they're just gonna have to do a hoist,
and that's certainly not the first choice
for an injured personnel.
- [Jarrett] Had he actually sustained injury,
he'd be cold, wet, injured, and alone.
But today, his spirits are a little higher.
- [Airman] I will hear what he's hearing.
I'm pretty psyched to get hoisted up into a helicopter,
that's somethin' I've only done once, so
it's somethin' I don't get to do often.
- [Man On Radio] Code 5-4 expect pickup north sideline.
- [Jarrett] Despite his excitement, the mission holds
real world value when it comes to exercising and measuring
contingency operational effectiveness.
- [Airman] I think this will be an excellent opportunity
to work with the JASDF and to see how that would go,
working together, and I imagine it's gonna go pretty well.
- [Jarrett] This exercise is a way to evaluate the readiness
of the Air Force and Koku-Jieitai if a pilot were to
actually eject from his aircraft.
- It's really important we do training like this
to be able to assess our capability to work with the JASDF
who are our hosts here in the country.
So, they are the rescue asset for us and if something
were to happen, time can be pretty critical
as far as rescue timing.
- [Jarrett] Once the Japanese pararescuemen patch him up,
he's then sent to the nearest capable medical facility
for further diagnostics or treatment.
Senior Airman Jarrett Vickers, Misawa Air Base, Japan.

pass_reason: training drill presented as training, no real rescue or outcome
